usdRate.sourceName: Reserve Bank of Australia, AUD/USD 0.7040 (Kiribati uses the Australian dollar)

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Kiribati National Statistics Office, CPI March 2026
inflation_cpi.note: All-items index 110.32 (Mar 2025) to 111.04 (Mar 2026). IMF puts 2025 average CPI at 6.5% and projects 4.5% for 2026.

inflation_projection.sourceName: IMF 2026 Article IV (2024-26 CPI 2.5%, 6.5%, 4.5%); Australian dollar user
inflation_projection.note: Kiribati uses the Australian dollar (RBA target 2-3%) but imported food and fuel kept its CPI near 4-5% on average over the last five years, so 4% is a rounded planning figure.

policy_rate.note: Kiribati has no central bank or monetary policy of its own; it uses the Australian dollar, so the Reserve Bank of Australia cash rate applies indirectly.

savings_account_rate.note: Only a commercial bank's own rate sheet publishes this (about 0.10% in Sep 2026); company pages are not used as sources and no central bank or statistics office publishes deposit rates for Kiribati.

fdr_3m_rate.note: Only a commercial bank's own rate sheet publishes this (about 0.60% for 90-179 days in Sep 2026); company pages are not used as sources and no official deposit rate series exists for Kiribati.

fdr_1y_rate.note: Only a commercial bank's own rate sheet publishes this (about 1.15% for 12 months in Sep 2026); company pages are not used as sources and no official deposit rate series exists for Kiribati.

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product found on Kiribati bank rate sheets.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No published weighted average deposit rate (no central bank; World Bank FR.INR.DPST has no Kiribati value).

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Kiribati government does not sell savings certificates or retail bonds.

tbill_91d_rate.note: Kiribati has no domestic treasury bill market.

tbond_5y_rate.note: Kiribati has no domestic government bond market.

tbond_10y_rate.note: Kiribati has no domestic government bond market.

tax_bank_interest.note: Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2009 s79A exempts the first A$250 of an individual's bank interest; the rest is taxed at the personal scale. No flat withholding rate on residents' interest found.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate exists in Kiribati.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: No deposit insurance scheme found for Kiribati (searched ADB Pacific finance sector brief, Ministry of Finance); likely none.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No legal cap or published credit card rate found for Kiribati.

equity_return_low.sourceName: No local stock market; global equity index in Australian dollar terms
equity_return_low.note: Low case for a global index fund held in AUD after weak decades and currency swings.

equity_return_base.sourceName: Global equity in AUD, capped at the local safe rate (about 1% on 12-month deposits) plus 4 points
equity_return_base.note: Kiribati has no stock exchange, so equity means a global index held in AUD; the base is held to the roughly 1% safe rate plus about 4 points.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Long-run global equity return in AUD terms
equity_return_high.note: High case close to the long-run nominal return of global equities in Australian dollars.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold in AUD; long-run USD gold trend and AUD/USD rate
gold_return_low.note: Gold can stagnate for a decade in real terms; low case barely positive in AUD.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold in AUD; long-run USD gold trend about 5% plus little expected AUD depreciation
gold_return_base.note: Kiribati uses the Australian dollar, so gold return is the USD gold trend with no big local currency depreciation.

gold_return_high.note: High case for a strong gold decade or AUD weakness.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: Local 12-month term deposits pay about 1% (bank rate sheets, Sep 2026; not cited as they are company pages); no government bills or bonds (IMF 2026 Article IV)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case near current savings and short deposit rates (about 0.1-0.6%).

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: Local 12-month term deposits pay about 1% (bank rate sheets, Sep 2026; not cited as they are company pages); no government bills or bonds (IMF 2026 Article IV)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base close to the roughly 1% 12-month deposit rate; the first A$250 of interest is tax-exempt, so tax drag is small for most savers.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Local 12-month term deposits pay about 1% (bank rate sheets, Sep 2026; not cited as they are company pages); no government bills or bonds (IMF 2026 Article IV)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case if Australian-linked deposit rates rise.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: No insurance regulator statistics on claim settlement published for Kiribati.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: No published pure term life premium rates in Kiribati; the state insurer holds a statutory monopoly (Insurance Act 1981) and publishes no rate tables.

health_hospitalisation_cost.sourceName: Government of Kiribati statement to UN Commission on Population and Development (2024)
health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Government statement: health care is free for all cases treatable locally, with overseas referral for non-terminal patients; out-of-pocket share is about 3% of health spending. Source dated 2024 (older than 2025).

health_premium_table.note: No private health insurance market found in Kiribati; public care is free.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Headline CPI planning rate; public health care is free
goal_inflation_health.note: No medical CPI is published and public care is free, so health costs are planned at the headline 4% assumption.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Headline CPI planning rate; schooling is free and compulsory
goal_inflation_education.note: No education CPI is published; education is free in public schools, so the headline 4% assumption is used.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via Measured World
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source reproducing UN WPP 2024; ages 60 and 70 and sex breakdown not found (WHO GHO API unavailable).

support_ratio.sourceName: UN WPP 2024 medium variant via PopulationPyramid.net; World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 7.14 (2025, World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL), 9.8 (2040) and 15.5 (2065, populationpyramid.net/kiribati/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: ISSA country profile: Kiribati (policies as of 1 January 2022)
retirement_age_default.note: No statutory pension age; the Kiribati Provident Fund pays its old-age lump sum from age 50 (early withdrawal at 45 if retired). Policies as of 1 January 2022 (older than 2025).

retirement_age_government.note: A 2016 amendment reportedly raised the public-service retirement age from 50 to 55, but the act on PacLII returns 403 and no other source could be read to confirm it.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: Local 12-month term deposits pay about 1% (bank rate sheets, Sep 2026; not cited as they are company pages); no government bills or bonds (IMF 2026 Article IV)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case near short deposit rates.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: Local 12-month term deposits pay about 1% (bank rate sheets, Sep 2026; not cited as they are company pages); no government bills or bonds (IMF 2026 Article IV)
retirement_return_base.note: Held at about the 1% 12-month deposit rate, the best safe rate available locally.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Local 12-month term deposits pay about 1% (bank rate sheets, Sep 2026; not cited as they are company pages); no government bills or bonds (IMF 2026 Article IV)
retirement_return_high.note: High case if deposit rates rise or part is held in higher-yield deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Kiribati Provident Fund crediting rate (ISSA 2022 profile: 5% in 2017, board reviews yearly, minimum 4%; fund site shows 5.5% for FY2021-22)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a mix of local deposits and global funds.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Kiribati Provident Fund crediting rate (ISSA 2022 profile: 5% in 2017, board reviews yearly, minimum 4%; fund site shows 5.5% for FY2021-22)
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: A balanced mix of about 1% deposits and about 5% global equity in AUD gives roughly 3.5%, below the provident fund's recent crediting rate.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Kiribati Provident Fund crediting rate (ISSA 2022 profile: 5% in 2017, board reviews yearly, minimum 4%; fund site shows 5.5% for FY2021-22)
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case in line with the provident fund's recent crediting rate.

old_age_allowance_monthly.sourceName: Government of Kiribati statement to UN Commission on Population and Development (2024)
old_age_allowance_monthly.note: The government's 2024 statement says citizens aged 60 and over receive $100 a fortnight, i.e. about A$217 a month (100 x 26 / 12). Source dated 2024 (older than 2025); the 2020 Act and later budget figures could not be read directly.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: Government of Kiribati statement to UN Commission on Population and Development (2024)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Statement: senior citizens aged 60 and over are entitled to the allowance; no means test is mentioned. ISSA 2022 still lists the older 2004 rule (age 65, A$50-60 a month), which the 2024 government statement supersedes. Source dated 2024 (older than 2025).

gratuity_rule.note: No general end-of-service gratuity law found; the Employment and Industrial Relations Code 2015 provides redundancy severance whose formula (s100) could not be verified.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: ISSA country profile: Kiribati (policies as of 1 January 2022)
public_pension_scheme.note: Kiribati Provident Fund: employees and employers each pay 7.5% of gross wages; paid as a lump sum (not a pension) from age 50; interest set yearly by the board (5% in 2017 per ISSA; fund site shows 5.5% for FY2021-22). ISSA profile is as of 2022 (older than 2025).

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificates or retail bonds.

equity_fund.note: No stock exchange or locally sold retail funds; only foreign funds bought abroad.

gold.note: No local bullion dealers; gold would have to be bought abroad.

pensionScheme.name: Kiribati Provident Fund
pensionScheme.note: Mandatory provident fund for employees; lump sum from age 50.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Ministry of Women, Youth, Sports and Social Affairs (Senior Citizens Allowance)
oldAgeAllowance.note: Universal allowance for citizens 60+; the ministry has no separate website, so this links to the government portal.

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry of Health and Medical Services
publicHealthCover.note: Free public health care, with overseas referral.
